messages:
Alicia Nguyen: FYI incoming support ticket from AcmeMaps — they report a sudden spike in 429s during a promo blast ~10:30 UTC. They say it started after their campaign kickoff and is still ongoing. Attaching their sample response.
Raj Patel: Can you paste the full response headers they saw? 429 body + x-rate-limit headers usually tell us which bucket was hit.
Alicia Nguyen: Here is the redacted response they sent:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 30000
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 167
x-rate-limit-scope: customer:acct_XXXX
content-type: application/json

{"error":"rate_exceeded","message":"requests per minute exceeded"}
```
They also included this curl repro (redacted token):
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","model":"rw-large","input":"...","max_tokens":512}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Mei Chen: Thanks — that scope shows customer bucket. Two quick checks: 1) was this a single client or many clients behind a single API key? 2) do we have any recent promo changes on quota or burst settings? Also, do we have a related spike in concurrent connections or token throughput? :eyes:
Alicia Nguyen: AcmeMaps says they have many end users but a single API key for the campaign. They did a 1-hour campaign, heavy parallelism from their side.
Sam Ortiz: I pulled their usage from BigQuery for the window 10:20–10:45 UTC. It's a sharp spike from ~5 req/s to ~240 req/s sustained for ~12 minutes, then a tail. Token throughput also went up 6x. I put the query and a small chart in the incident board.
RateLimitBot: Alert: 429-rate-increase detected for customer acct_XXXX — 5x baseline. More details: routes impacted: /v1/generate (80%), /v1/embeddings (15%), other (5%).
Raj Patel: Ok. Likely quota exhaustion (customer-level token or req/min). Two possible behaviors: we apply a token-bucket per-customer plus per-route soft-limits and a global safety limiter. When customer bucket empties they get 429 with that x-rate-limit headers. Need to confirm which limiter tripped.
Mei Chen: Can you check the rate-limiter debug logs for that customer id around 10:28:00? The runtime logs include limiter_id and rule_name. Use log query:
```
resource.type="gke_cluster"
labels.cluster_name="redwood-runtime-prod"
jsonPayload.customer_id="acct_XXXX"
jsonPayload.severity="WARN"
jsonPayload.component="rate_limiter"
timestamp >= "2026-03-08T10:20:00Z" AND timestamp <= "2026-03-08T10:40:00Z"
```
Sam Ortiz: Pulled a sample entry:
```
{"ts":"2026-03-08T10:27:58Z","component":"rate_limiter","customer":"acct_XXXX","rule":"customer_token_per_min","limit":30000,"remaining":0,"action":"throttle"}
```
Alicia Nguyen: Good catch. That matches the x-rate-limit header. Customer token-per-minute hit zero.
Raj Patel: For observability follow-up we should: 1) add a dashboard panel breaking 429s by limiter (customer_token_per_min, route_qps, global_safety) 2) surface token consumption by customer in a rate chart, 3) add an anomaly alert on token burn rate that triggers before remaining==0.
Mei Chen: Agreed. Suggested PromQL for alert (rough draft) to detect rapid token depletion by customer over 2m:
```
increase(redwood_customer_tokens_consumed_total{customer_id="acct_XXXX"}[2m]) > 0.8 * (quota_tokens_per_min{customer_id="acct_XXXX"})
```
Raj Patel: Nice. We should avoid per-customer hard-coded rules in Prom but create a template alert that interpolates customer id via the alerting UI. Also add a composite alert that looks for 429 spike + token_remaining==0.
Alicia Nguyen: For the immediate customer-facing fix, can we offer AcmeMaps a temporary quota bump or a per-minute soft increase so their campaign finishes? Also propose they throttle client concurrency.
Mei Chen: Yes — product can approve a temporary bump. But let's document reproducible steps so support can replicate and confirm fixes. Repro steps I recommend:
1) Use their API key with the same parallelism (nr_workers=60) and same payload size. Example harness:
```
for i in $(seq 1 60); do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
2) Watch x-rate-limit-* headers in responses
3) Tail rate_limiter logs for rule hits
Sam Ortiz: Also tested a smoothing change locally: if we switch customer_token_bucket to a leaky-bucket with burst_capacity=2x baseline, the 12-minute campaign would not have hit 0, but that increases cost. We can propose a one-time burst_policy change for AcmeMaps: burst_factor=2 for 15m.
Raj Patel: Make sure to capture attribution data in the dashboard so when we change policy we can measure cost impact (tokens consumed vs expected). Add a panel: tokens_consumed_total / (quota_tokens_per_min * minutes) by customer.
Alicia Nguyen: Messaging to customer drafted: short-term: temporary bump (approved), recommended client-side concurrency limit, and a postmortem with dashboards. I'll send now.
Mei Chen: I'll own the dashboard changes. Plan:
- New panel: 429 rate by limiter name and route (time series)
- New panel: token remaining by customer (gauge + histogram)
- New panel: concurrent connections per API key
- New composite alert: (429-rate increase by >5x) AND (token_remaining==0) -> page SRE

Raj Patel: For attribution, ensure logs include model and route tags. Runtime already attaches labels model=rw-large and route=/v1/generate. Use them in Grafana queries: group by customer_id, model, route.
RateLimitBot: Action logged: temporary_quota_bump acct_XXXX +50% for 20 minutes by Mei Chen
Alicia Nguyen: Customer replied: "Thanks — bump worked, campaign finished, seeing some failures but much fewer 429s. Can you share the dashboard?"
Mei Chen: Shared dashboard link in thread (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/rate-limit-attrib (internal only). Follow-ups: convert the draft PromQL into an alert rule, add a playbook entry for campaign customers with guidance on concurrency and recommended pre-bumps.
Sam Ortiz: I'll add a quick script in support playbooks/examples: `simulate_campaign.sh` and a quick-made Prometheus recording rule to compute per-customer burn-rate.
Raj Patel: Post-incident ownership: SRE will add the composite alert and dashboard, Product will own the burst-policy templates, Support will own playbook and customer communication. Assigning owners: Raj (SRE), Mei (Product), Alicia (Support), Sam (DevEx).
Alicia Nguyen: Closing notes to ticket: temporary bump applied, customer validated, dashboards and alerts are next-day work items. I've scheduled a follow-up with AcmeMaps for 48h to review costs.
Mei Chen: Thanks all :raised_hands: I'll ping once dashboard is live.
Raj Patel: Good job triaging. Long term we should consider: auto-detect campaign patterns and suggest pre-bump + client-rate-limits. Also record model-level attribution — some models chew more tokens so route attribution alone isn't enough.
Alicia Nguyen: Adding that to the roadmap item in product board. End of thread.
